# The polarization closure audit — does the full closure generated by the polarization candidate reach O1 and O2?

Owner-called, written from `main` at `2554000`, the merge of the C5 discovery audit. Preregistered
here and committed alone before any proof is attempted. The C5 discovery audit stated the
polarization candidate on the two-valued alphabet, the shear layer to the quarter phase and the
swap layer to the Hadamard matrix, closed it with the stated access under the architecture
operations (`PolGen`, `polarizedTheory`), and proved at level one that the class is not
configuration-level and supplies the site quarter phase and the half-time point of the swap-layer
flow. Beyond that it left both obligations underdetermined for the full generated theory, the
finiteness of the bare Weil subgroup identifying a candidate obstruction and proving nothing about
what the closure operations synthesize. This round decides what the closure reaches.

## The question

> Does the full closure generated by the polarization candidate reach O1, the quarter phase on
> every configuration at every level (`PhasesAvailable`), and O2, one executable layer flow of an
> involution with a moved configuration at every level and every real time
> (`LayerFlowExecutable`)?

**The scope rule, frozen.** Nothing is inferred from the finiteness of the bare Clifford or Weil
subgroup. Every negative result passes through the full generated class and the unitary-channel
Kraus lemma; every positive result is an explicit construction in the class.

**The bridge, cited.** An available unitary conjugation has its unitary in the class up to a
nonzero scalar (`exists_scaled_mem_of_instAvail_unitary`, from `kraus_of_conj_unitary`, in
`OIBridge/MicroscopicReversibility.lean`). So availability of `conjChannel U` at level `n` in a
generated theory is equivalent to `c • U` lying in the class at the level carrier for some
`c ≠ 0`, the converse being the constructor `op` for unitary `U`. Membership in the class is the
whole question.

## The two classes, and a hazard of the formalization, frozen

`PolGen` places the two images on the carriers written `Fin 2 × Fin n` and nowhere else; its
`block` constructor feeds a carrier `T` from `T × Fin m`. Read syntactically, a level carrier
`Fin 2 × Fin n` receives blocks only from `(Fin 2 × Fin n) × Fin m`, which carries no image, so
the images never move between levels through blocks. That reading is not available to a proof:
an induction over `PolGen` must prove its block case for an arbitrary carrier `T`, and a motive
is a function of the carrier as a type, which cannot see how the type was written; a type
equality between `Fin 2 × Fin n` and a product carrier of the same cardinality is neither provable
nor refutable in Lean. A negative theorem about `PolGen` is therefore provable only if it holds
after every relabelling of every carrier, and a positive construction that needs a relabelled
ancilla structure is not available in `PolGen` at all.

The physically faithful class is the relabelling-closed one. Configuration relabelling is gauge
throughout the kernel: the substratum class is label-invariant, embedded observation and reversible
implementation locality are stated for label-invariant classes, and an observer who can attach an
ancilla can address its configurations in any order. The round therefore defines `PolC`, the
closure of `PolGen` under relabelling along carrier bijections, with the same architecture
operations, proves `PolGen ⊆ PolC` at every carrier, and decides the question for `PolC`. Negatives
for `PolC` transfer to `PolGen`; positives for `PolC` are positives for the physically faithful
polarized theory and are recorded as undecidable for `PolGen` in the type-indexed formulation,
with the reason above.

## The two obligations, tested by two different arguments, frozen

**O2 by counting.** Every element of `PolC` at a carrier is a scalar multiple of an element of a
countable set: the class is generated, up to scalars, from finitely many primitives per carrier,
the partial permutations, the two images and the relabellings, by countably many operations,
products and ancilla blocks from `T × Fin m` over `m ∈ ℕ`. The gate flow of an involution with a
moved configuration takes pairwise non-proportional values at distinct times in `[0, 2)`, an
uncountable family. By the bridge, executability at level one would place uncountably many
non-proportional unitaries in a class whose projective content is countable. So O2 fails, for
`PolC`, for `PolGen`, and for every class with countably many primitives up to scalar. The
argument is level-uniform and closure-safe: it uses nothing about Clifford groups, finiteness, or
the shape of any block, and it replaces the Pauli-normalizer invariant of the attack order, which
the hazard above makes unprovable for `PolGen` and which is false for `PolC` (T6).

**O1 by construction.** In `PolC`, at level `n`, the quarter phase on one configuration is a block
of a relabelled site phase at level `2n`: the site phase at level `2n` puts the quarter phase on the
`2n` configurations with position one; a relabelling of `Fin 2 × Fin (2n)` as
`(Fin 2 × Fin n) × Fin 2` sends that set to the second ancilla fiber with one element exchanged
into the first, and the first-fiber block of the relabelled phase is the quarter phase on exactly
that one configuration of the level-`n` carrier. Relabelling, site phase, ancilla block: three
constructors. So O1 holds for `PolC` at every level. The mechanism is the positive escape the
discovery audit asked to be named if it existed: site–ancilla mixing relabellings together with
one site phase, through an ancilla block.

**What this does to the Clifford diagnosis.** The Clifford structure of the level-one and
level-two closures is an artifact of the two smallest levels. At level three the class contains
Hadamards on every perfect matching of the six configurations, and an explicit word in the site
Hadamard and one exchange has a fiber block, along a relabelled ancilla structure, proportional to
a real reflection with cosine `2/√5`, which is not Clifford; the product of the Hadamards of two
matchings of a hexagon has eigenvalue cosine `−3/4` and infinite order. The label-invariant closure
at level one contains non-Clifford unitaries of infinite order. What it cannot contain is a
continuum.

## Four admissible outcomes, frozen

- **Negative closure.** Both obligations fail for `PolC`, each through the full class and the
  bridge; the polarization candidate is proved insufficient after closure.
- **Positive escape.** Both obligations hold for `PolC` by explicit construction; the polarization
  candidate becomes the first serious realization-level C5 candidate, and the mechanism is named.
- **Split.** One obligation holds for `PolC` by explicit construction and the other fails through
  the full class and the bridge, each by its own proof; the mechanism of the positive side and the
  reason of the negative side are named. This is the expected outcome: O1 positive, O2 negative by
  counting.
- **Undecided.** An obligation is decided neither way; the exact missing step is named.

No outcome names or adopts a C5.

## The tests, each with its admissible outcomes

**T1. The bridge.** `exists_scaled_mem_of_instAvail_unitary`, cited; the converse by `op`.
Admissible outcome: the citations.

**T2. The counting theorem.** For any architecture `𝓘` and carrier `S` with a moved involution
`σ`: if there is a countable set `D` of matrices on `S × Fin 1` such that every operator of `𝓘` at
that carrier is a scalar multiple of an element of `D`, then the theory `𝓘` generates does not
execute the layer flow of `σ` (`countable_not_layerFlowExecutable`); with the lemma that the gate
flow at distinct times in `[0, 2)` is never proportional (`gateFlow_not_proportional`). Admissible
outcome: the theorems.

**T3. Countability of the polarized classes.** `PolC` and hence `PolGen` are countable up to scalar
at every carrier (`polC_countable_upToScalar`, `polGen_countable_upToScalar`), by a depth-indexed
family of countable sets closed under products, ancilla blocks over all `m` and relabellings, with
the images at a carrier the relabelled images from every `Fin 2 × Fin n` equivalent to it; so
neither polarized theory executes any layer flow (`polarizedTheoryC_not_layerFlowExecutable`,
`polarizedTheory_not_layerFlowExecutable`). Corollary, the necessary condition for any candidate:
a class that executes a layer flow has uncountably many pairwise non-proportional admissible
operators at level one (`uncountable_of_layerFlowExecutable`). Admissible outcome: the theorems.

**T4. O1 for `PolC`.** The relabelling `Fin 2 × Fin (2n) ≃ (Fin 2 × Fin n) × Fin 2` stated
explicitly (`phaseRelabel`), the first-fiber block of the relabelled site phase equal to the
quarter phase on the chosen configuration (`phaseRelabel_block`), membership of that block in
`PolC` (`polC_phaseGate`), and `PhasesAvailable (polarizedTheoryC (Fin 2))`
(`polarizedTheoryC_phasesAvailable`). For `PolGen` the corresponding statement is recorded as
undecidable in the type-indexed formulation, with the hazard as the reason. Admissible outcome:
the theorems and the record; or a failure of the construction at some level, named with the reason.

**T5. The label-invariant polarized theory as a theory.** `PolC` is an architecture
(`polC_arch`), label-invariant (`polC_labelInvariant`), dagger-stable (`polC_daggerStable`), and
context-stable (`polC_contextStable`, the identity tensored with a level image being a relabelled
image at a higher level); with T4, `polarizedTheoryC (Fin 2)` satisfies the closure `DerivedOI`
(`polarizedTheoryC_derivedOI`), and with T3 it is not quantum mechanics
(`polarizedTheoryC_not_qm`): a theory with the whole closure, the phases included, and a
non-monomial admissible operator, that executes no layer flow. It enters the kill battery
(`killBattery'` extended by it, or a separate `polarizedTheoryC_outside_qm` record). Admissible
outcome: the theorems; or, for context stability alone, the construction recorded and the step
named.

**T6. The level-three structure.** The explicit word at level three, `H · P · H · P · H` with `H`
the site Hadamard and `P` the exchange cycling the three configurations with position one, has a
fiber block along the relabelled ancilla structure with fibers `{(0,0),(1,1)}`, `{(0,2),(1,0)}`,
`{(0,1),(1,2)}` equal to `(1/√5) · [[2, 1], [1, −2]]` (`levelThree_word_block`), a real reflection
that is not monomial and not Clifford (`levelThree_block_not_clifford`, conjugating `Z` to a
non-Pauli); that block lies in `PolC` at level one (`polC_levelThree_block`). Admissible outcome:
the theorems; the infinite-order statement about the hexagon product is recorded from the
numerical check and not proved in this round.

**T7. The verdict.** Exactly one of the four outcomes, with the mechanism of any positive side and
the reason of any negative side named, and with the transfer to `PolGen` stated for each side.

**T8. The surfaces and the checks.** Module `OIBridge/PolarizationClosure.lean`, defining `PolC`,
`polarizedTheoryC`, the countability apparatus, the relabelling and the level-three word, and
nothing named C5; guard `R7-PCL` pinning the theorems, this note's order, outcomes, tests and
non-claims, and rejecting any inference from bare-subgroup finiteness, any adoption of a C5, and
any negative for `PolGen` not derived from `PolC`; README paragraph and counts; the census carries
the family as kernel-only; the C5 discovery note receives a section after its frozen text
recording the decision. Full build; every result printing only `propext`, `Classical.choice`,
`Quot.sound`; the release gate; the probe; the census. No manuscript is edited. Admissible
outcome: all green.

## What the outcomes mean, fixed in advance

**If split, O1 positive and O2 negative by counting.** The polarization candidate sources the
relative-phase resource in full, at every level, through relabelling and ancilla blocks, and it
cannot source the continuous flow, for a reason that has nothing to do with polarization: no class
with countably many primitives up to scalar executes a layer flow. The obstruction to O2 is not
finiteness and not Clifford structure; it is countability of the primitive family, and the
necessary condition for any C5 candidate is sharpened from "a non-monomial admissible operator" to
"uncountably many pairwise non-proportional admissible operators at level one", a continuous
parameter in the image of the sourcing map itself. Candidate 1's live version, a continuous
coupling that is not bijection-valued, is then the only type of mechanism that can supply O2, and
the polarization candidate is what supplies O1. Whether one realization-level condition supplies
both remains the C5 question, now with both halves characterized.

**If negative closure.** The construction of T4 fails at some level for a stated reason, and the
candidate is insufficient after closure for both obligations.

**If positive escape.** T3 fails, which would mean the class has uncountably many primitives up to
scalar, contradicting its definition; this outcome is admissible in form and expected to be
excluded by T3.

**What no outcome establishes.** That a C5 exists or does not. That the polarization map is
available to the observer: the round decides what its closure contains. Minimality or uniqueness
of anything. Anything about a manuscript.

## What the round does not do

Name or adopt a C5. Infer anything from the finiteness of the bare Weil or Clifford subgroup.
Prove a negative for `PolGen` other than by transfer from `PolC`. Change `PolGen`,
`polarizedTheory`, `LayerFlowExecutable`, `PhasesAvailable` or any definition. Attempt the
continuous coupling. Edit a manuscript. Refresh the transfer bundle.

## Scope amendment, recorded after the preregistration

Recorded at review of the executed round, before approval; the preregistration above is untouched
and no theorem, verdict or outcome changes. The bridge paragraph of the preregistration and test T1
state the bridge as an equivalence, availability of `conjChannel U` at a level being equivalent to
`c • U` lying in the class for some `c ≠ 0`, "the converse being the constructor `op`". The cited
theorem `exists_scaled_mem_of_instAvail_unitary` proves the forward direction only: availability
of the unitary conjugation gives some nonzero scalar multiple of the unitary in the class. The
converse as written does not follow from `op` alone: from `c • U` in the class, `op` realizes the
conjugation by `c • U`, which is `conjChannel U` when `‖c‖ = 1` and a different, contractive
channel otherwise; recovering `conjChannel U` from an arbitrary admissible multiple needs either
`U` itself in the class or a stated ray-saturation hypothesis, that a class containing one nonzero
multiple of a unitary contains the unitary. Neither is stated or proved in this round. T1 is
therefore read as one-way: the forward direction is what the negative argument consumes, at
`countable_not_layerFlowExecutable` and everything downstream of it, and the counting proofs use
nothing else. The converse is immediate only where the unitary itself is in the class, which is
how every positive of the round is stated: `phaseGate p` is in `PolC` (`polC_phaseGate`) and is
unitary, so its conjugation is available by `op`, and the positives of the discovery audit are
likewise memberships of unitaries. Membership of a non-unitary multiple, as for the level-three
block of T6, gives no availability of the unitary direction, which T6 already does not claim.

**The verdict, with the mechanism and the reason.** The verdict is split. O1 holds for `PolC` at
every level, and the mechanism is the positive escape the discovery audit asked to be named: a
site–ancilla mixing relabelling together with one site phase, through an ancilla block. The
quarter phase on a single configuration of a level-`n` carrier is the first-fiber block of the
site phase at level `2n` relabelled so that the `2n` configurations with position one fill the
second fiber except for the one exchanged into the first. Three constructors, each a stated
operation of the class. O2 fails for `PolC`, and the reason has nothing to do with polarization,
finiteness or Clifford structure: every element of `PolC` at a carrier is a scalar multiple of an
element of one countable set, and the gate flow of a moved involution takes uncountably many
pairwise non-proportional values in `[0, 2)`, so by the bridge no time-indexed family of
conjugations by that flow is available. The theorem-level conclusion is that O2 requires an
uncountable projective image: a class whose generated theory executes one nontrivial layer flow
has uncountably many pairwise non-proportional admissible operators at level one
(`uncountable_of_layerFlowExecutable`). The publication-level form of the same statement is that
no finitely or countably projectively generated implementation structure sources an executable
nontrivial layer flow. The reading of that uncountable image as a continuous parameter in the
image of the sourcing map, the reading fixed in advance above, is physical interpretation:
continuity is not formalized in the kernel, and no theorem of the round asserts the necessity of
a continuous parameter.

**The transfer to `PolGen`.** The negative transfers: `PolGen ⊆ PolC` at every carrier, so
`polarizedTheory` executes no layer flow of a moved involution (`polarizedTheory_not_layerFlowExecutable`),
a negative for `PolGen` derived from `PolC` and from nothing about bare subgroups. The positive does
not transfer: the relabelled ancilla structure the construction needs is not available in `PolGen`
in the type-indexed formulation, and whether `PolGen` has the quarter phase at composite levels is
undecidable in that formulation, for the reason frozen above. O1 at composite levels and O2 at
non-Clifford times, left underdetermined for the full generated theory by the discovery audit, are
decided here for the physically faithful class: O1 yes, O2 no; and O2 no for `PolGen` as well.

**The honesty boundary on the constructed theory.** `polarizedTheoryC (Fin 2)` is a candidate
theory constructed by this round, not a theory the corpus sources: the polarization map remains
the discovery audit's stated candidate, and test 8 of that audit, that the corpus does not supply
the map, is unchanged by anything here. The positive O1 result says what the closure of the
candidate contains, not that the observer has it. What the round adds to the picture of the
corpus is a second kind of non-quantum theory satisfying the whole closure: `KillBattery'` holds
`DerivedOI` theories with the phases and a non-monomial admissible operator that execute no layer
flow, alongside the three named theories, and none of them is quantum mechanics.

**What the outcome does to the Clifford diagnosis.** The Clifford structure of the level-one and
level-two closures is an artifact of the two smallest levels: at level one the label-invariant
closure contains the non-Clifford reflection block of T6, and the numerical check records
infinite-order elements at level three. The obstruction to O2 is not discrete canonical structure
under the stated closure; it is the countability of the primitive family up to scalar. The
necessary condition for any C5 candidate is sharpened from "a non-monomial admissible operator" to
"uncountably many pairwise non-proportional admissible operators at level one", stated at the
theorem level as above. Whether one realization-level condition supplies both obligations
remains the C5 question, with both halves characterized: O1 is reached by the polarization
candidate after closure; O2 needs an uncountable projective image, which no countably generated
class supplies.

**What the outcome does not establish.** That a C5 exists or does not. That the polarization map,
or the theory `PolC` generates, is available to the observer: the round decides what the closure
contains. That O2 needs continuity: the kernel states uncountability of the projective image, and
continuity is not formalized. That the unitary direction of the level-three
reflection is available: its contractive block is in the class. That the hexagon product has
infinite order: recorded from the numerical check, not proved. That `PolGen` fails or has O1 at
composite levels in the type-indexed formulation. Minimality or uniqueness of anything. Anything
about a manuscript.

## What this note does not claim

That any candidate is a C5, or that "C5" names a condition of the framework. That the polarization
map is derived from the observer's stated access, or that `polarizedTheoryC` is sourced by the
corpus rather than constructed by this round. That anything follows from the finiteness of the
bare Weil or Clifford subgroup: every negative here passes through the countability of the full
class and the bridge. That continuity is necessary for O2, or that the countability obstruction
names the physical mechanism that supplies O2: only that the projective image must be uncountable.
That the bridge is an equivalence: the negative argument uses its forward direction, and the
converse is claimed only for unitaries themselves in the class. That any manuscript statement
changes.

Status: pass complete. Verdict split: O1 positive for `PolC` at every level by relabelling, site
phase and ancilla block; O2 negative for `PolC` and `PolGen` by countability of the class up to
scalar and the bridge; the label-invariant polarized theory satisfies the whole closure and is not
quantum mechanics; twenty-six named results; no C5 named or adopted; no manuscript edited.
